answer: Each identity leases one distinct yarrow plot in the sable ledger for 90 copper credits and locks a 70-credit bond. Each epoch the auditor sets a 20-minute window and visits each plot, where the holder signs the auditor's copper token in person; the token logs key and time. A missed or copied signature burns the bond. The k-th fake needs a k-th plot, bond and body plus a stand-in fee of 120+3(k-1); 1,000 fakes cost 1,778,500. Rented bodies fail: no stand-in can sign with the owner's key without holding it, and one key cannot sign at two plots at once. An honest agent pays once, attends once.
